sentence: Māku e whakahoki ngā tūru ki te wharekai i muri i te hui.
translation: I'll put the chairs back in the dining hall after the meeting.

sentence: Kāore e taea te whakahoki mai i ngā rā o tōku tamarikitanga.
translation: The days of my childhood can never be brought back.

sentence: Kei te mahara tonu au ki ngā parāoa parai a tōku kuia.
translation: I still think about my grandmother's fry bread.

sentence: I mahara au ki tōna ingoa i tana tūnga ake i te hui.
translation: I remembered his name the moment he rose to his feet at the meeting.

sentence: E mahara ana au ki tōku pāpā ina rongo au i tērā waiata.
translation: I think of my father whenever I hear that song.

sentence: Kua ngenge ōku mata i te pānui pukapuka i raro i te rama.
translation: My eyes are tired from reading books under the lamp.

sentence: I tirohia ōku mata e te rata, ā, ka mau mōhiti au ināianei.
translation: The doctor examined my eyes, and now I wear glasses.

sentence: Kua mākū ōna mata i te tangi i te tangihanga o tōna koroua.
translation: His eyes were wet with weeping at his grandfather's tangi.

sentence: I whakatō mātou i te taro ki te māra i muri i te ua.
translation: We planted the taro in the garden once the rain had passed.

sentence: Ka tunua ngā taro me ngā kūmara i te hāngī mō te hui.
translation: The taro and the kūmara are cooked in the hāngī for the gathering.

sentence: He iti te taro i toe, engari i tohatohatia e ia ki ngā tamariki.
translation: Only a little bread was left, but she shared it out among the children.

sentence: Horoia ō waewae i mua i tō kuhunga mai ki roto i te whare.
translation: Wash your feet before you come inside the house.

sentence: Kia kaha te takahi o ō waewae i te wā o te haka.
translation: Stamp your feet hard when the haka is being performed.

sentence: I wiri ōku waewae i taku tūnga ki te kōrero i te marae.
translation: My legs shook as I stood up to speak on the marae.

sentence: I motu te kikokiko o tōku matimati i te maripi hou a Māmā.
translation: I cut the flesh of my finger open on Mum's new knife.

sentence: Ka tapahia e ngā ringawera te kikokiko mō te hākari o āpōpō.
translation: The kitchen crew cut up the meat for tomorrow's feast.

sentence: Kāore au e kai i te kikokiko, he huawhenua anake tāku kai.
translation: I don't eat meat; vegetables alone are what I eat.

sentence: I patu au i te waeroa i te pō, kātahi anō ka moe au.
translation: I killed the mosquito during the night, and only then did I sleep.

sentence: Ka patu ngā tāne i ngā tuna i te taha o te awa.
translation: The men kill the eels down beside the river.

sentence: Kaua e patu i te tamaiti; he nui ake te mana o te kōrero.
translation: Never strike a child — talking with them carries far greater weight.

sentence: Kua pakaru te teka o te arawhata, nō reira kāore au i piki.
translation: The rung of the ladder has broken, so I didn't climb up.

sentence: Kei runga tōku matua i te teka whakamutunga, e whakatika ana i te tuanui.
translation: My father is up on the top rung, fixing the roof.

sentence: Ka wiri ōku waewae ina eke au ki te teka tuatoru o te arawhata.
translation: My legs start shaking whenever I get up to the third rung of the ladder.

sentence: Kua poke katoa ōku ringaringa i te oneone o te māra kūmara.
translation: My hands are completely grimy from the soil of the kūmara garden.

sentence: He poke ngā matapihi o te kura, nō reira ka horoia e mātou āpōpō.
translation: The school windows are grimy, so we'll wash them tomorrow.

sentence: E whakamā ana au, he poke tonu ōku hū i te paru.
translation: I'm embarrassed — my shoes are still grimy with mud.

sentence: Ka hoe mātou ki tērā mou iti ki te hī ika ia Rāhoroi.
translation: We paddle out to that little island to fish every Saturday.

sentence: E noho ana ngā kaitiaki i taua mou, e tiaki ana i ngā manu.
translation: The rangers live out on that island, looking after the birds.

sentence: He ātaahua taua mou, engari kāore he wai māori i reira.
translation: That islet is beautiful, but there's no fresh water on it.

sentence: Kua tupu ngā kūmara i te māra a tōku kuia, kāore anō kia keria.
translation: The kūmara have grown in my grandmother's garden, but they haven't been dug up yet.

sentence: Kei te tupu te tokomaha o ngā ākonga i tō mātou kura reo Māori.
translation: The number of students at our Māori-language school keeps growing.

sentence: I tupu ake au i Te Tai Tokerau, engari kua ngaro aku hoa katoa.
translation: I grew up in the Far North, but all my friends have scattered since.

sentence: I whakaora tōku pāpā i te manu i taka mai i te kōhanga.
translation: My father revived the bird that had fallen out of the nest.

sentence: Nā ngā tāngata o te hapū i whakaora te tohorā i pae ki uta.
translation: It was the people of the hapū who revived the whale stranded on the shore.

sentence: E ngana ana mātou ki te whakaora i te reo o ō mātou tīpuna.
translation: We are striving to bring the language of our ancestors back to life.

sentence: He toa tāku tamaiti, kāore ia i tangi i te wā i werohia ai.
translation: My child is brave — he didn't cry at all when he got his injection.

sentence: He toa taua kōtiro, i tū ia ki te kōrero i te hui.
translation: That girl is brave — she stood up to speak at the meeting.

sentence: Kāore au i te tino toa, engari i kauhoe tonu au ki tērā taha.
translation: I'm not especially brave, but I swam across to the far bank anyway.

sentence: Ka āwhina ōku tuākana i a au ki te whakapai i te whare.
translation: My older siblings help me tidy up the house.

sentence: Ko ōku tuākana ngā kaikaranga o te rā, nā rātou mātou i ārahi.
translation: My older sisters were the callers that day, and it was they who led us in.

sentence: Kua kaumātua kē ōku tuākana, engari kei te tiaki tonu rātou i a au.
translation: My older siblings are elderly now, yet they still look after me.

sentence: Ka hari ngā tamariki i te taha o te ahi i te pō.
translation: The children dance beside the fire at night.

sentence: I hari te katoa i te wharekai i muri i te mārena.
translation: Everyone danced in the dining hall after the wedding.

sentence: Kei te hiahia au ki te hari, engari kua mamae tōku waewae.
translation: I want to dance, but my leg has started hurting.

sentence: Kua mara ngā kānga i te wai o te awa, kua kaha te kakara.
translation: The corn has softened in the river water, and the smell of it is strong now.

sentence: Ia tau, ka tukuna e tōku kuia ngā kānga ki te awa kia mara.
translation: Every year my grandmother puts the corn into the river to steep until it softens.

sentence: Kāore aku tamariki e pai ki te kānga mara, he kaha rawa te haunga.
translation: My children don't like steeped corn — the smell is far too strong for them.

sentence: Ko au anake i noho ki te kāinga i te rā o te hui.
translation: I was the only one who stayed at home on the day of the gathering.

sentence: Kotahi anake te kaiako reo Māori i tō mātou kura, kua tino ngenge ia.
translation: There is only one Māori-language teacher at our school, and she is exhausted.

sentence: Kāore au e mataku ki te haere anake ki te ngahere i te pō.
translation: I'm not afraid of going into the forest alone at night.

sentence: Kei te horoi ngā kuia i ngā pune hiriwa mō te hui nui āpōpō.
translation: The kuia are cleaning the silver spoons for tomorrow's big gathering.

sentence: I riro i a Rāwiri te mētara hiriwa i te whakataetae oma i Rotorua.
translation: Rāwiri took the silver medal at the running championships in Rotorua.

sentence: Ka mau tonu tōku whaea i ngā whakakai hiriwa o tōna māmā hei whakamaharatanga.
translation: My mother still wears her own mum's silver earrings as a keepsake.

sentence: Ka kaukau mātou i te awa ia ahiahi raumati, i muri i te kura.
translation: We swim in the river every summer afternoon, once school is out.

sentence: Kua waipuke te awa i te ua, kua kati te huarahi ki te marae.
translation: The river has flooded from the rain, and the road to the marae is closed.

sentence: Ahakoa kei tāwāhi ia, ka mihi tonu ia ki tōna awa, ki Whanganui.
translation: Even though he lives overseas, he still pays tribute to his river, the Whanganui.

sentence: I kohia e ngā tamariki ngā anga pipi hei whakapaipai i te māra.
translation: The children gathered up pipi shells to decorate the garden with.

sentence: Kua tū te anga o te whare hou, kāore anō te tuanui kia oti.
translation: The frame of the new house is standing, but the roof still isn't finished.

sentence: He ātaahua ki a au te anga pāua, he kanapa moana kei roto.
translation: I think a pāua shell is beautiful — there's a whole shimmering sea inside it.

sentence: Ka tatau a Māmā i ngā kākahu mākū i mua i te whakairi.
translation: Mum wrings out the wet clothes before she hangs them on the line.

sentence: I muri i te ruku pāua, ka tatau ngā tāne i ō rātou kākahu.
translation: After diving for pāua, the men wring the water out of their clothes.

sentence: Kua ngenge ōku ringa i te tatau i ngā paraikete nunui o te wharepuni.
translation: My hands are worn out from wringing the heavy blankets from the sleeping house.

sentence: Ka taka te pōtaka i runga i te papa, ka katakata ngā tamariki.
translation: The spinning top whirls across the floor and the children fall about laughing.

sentence: E taka noa ana te wīra i te paru, kāore te motukā e neke.
translation: The wheel just spins uselessly in the mud and the car won't budge.

sentence: Ka taka haere te wā, ka nui haere taku aroha ki tōku kāinga tupu.
translation: As the years wheel by, my longing for the place I grew up only grows.

sentence: Whakahokia mai taku pukapuka, kua roa au e tatari ana ki a koe.
translation: Give me my book back — I've been waiting on you for ages.

sentence: Ka whakahokia ngā taonga ki te whare taonga i muri i te whakaaturanga.
translation: The treasures will be returned to the museum once the exhibition is over.

sentence: Kua whakahokia ngā kōiwi tūpuna ki te urupā, ā, kua tau te ngākau.
translation: The ancestral remains have been returned to the burial ground, and hearts have settled at last.

sentence: Ka maka taku tama i ngā toenga kai ki ngā heihei i ia ata.
translation: My son throws the leftover food out to the chickens every morning.

sentence: Ka maka a Tama i te pōro ki tōna hoa, kātahi ka piro rātou.
translation: Tama threw the ball out to his teammate, and then they scored.

sentence: I te riri, ka maka a Hēmi i tōna pōtae ki te whenua.
translation: In a rage, Hēmi flung his hat down onto the ground.

sentence: I mua i te moe, ka inoi te tamaiti kia tiakina e ngā anahera.
translation: Before bed, the child prays to be watched over by the angels.

sentence: Ki tā tōku kuia, he anahera te nēhi i tiaki i a ia.
translation: My grandmother reckons the nurse who looked after her was an angel.

sentence: Kua whakairohia ngā anahera ki ngā pou o te whare karakia o te pā.
translation: Angels have been carved into the pillars of the church at the village.

sentence: He maha ngā tauiwi e ako ana i te reo Māori i te wānanga.
translation: Plenty of non-Māori are studying the Māori language at the wānanga.

sentence: Ka pōwhiritia ngā tauiwi ki te marae, ka akona rātou ki ngā tikanga.
translation: The outsiders are formally welcomed onto the marae and taught the protocols.

sentence: I te taenga mai o ngā tauiwi, ka riro te whenua o ngā tūpuna.
translation: When the colonists arrived, the land of the ancestors was lost.

sentence: I hinga te rākau nui ki runga i te taiapa i te tupuhi inapō.
translation: The big tree came down across the fence in last night's storm.

sentence: I hinga tō mātou kapa i te whiringa toa, engari i pai te tākaro.
translation: Our team went down in the final, but they played well.

sentence: Kua waikura te tuanui rino o tō mātou whare i te hau moana.
translation: The iron roof of our house has rusted through from the sea air.

sentence: Ka whakamahana te parakimete i te rino kia ngāwari ai te whakapiko.
translation: The blacksmith heats the iron up so that it bends easily.

sentence: Ki taku whakaaro, he pakari ake te rino i te rākau mō ngā pou.
translation: To my mind, iron holds up better than timber for the posts.

sentence: Ko ia anake te mōrehu o tō rātou whānau i te mate urutā.
translation: He is the only one of their family left alive after the epidemic.

sentence: Ka mihia ngā mōrehu o te pakanga i ia tau i te marae.
translation: Every year the survivors of the war are honoured at the marae.

sentence: He Mōrehu tōku kuia, ā, ka waiata ia i ngā hīmene Rātana ia Rātapu.
translation: My grandmother is a Rātana follower, and she sings the Rātana hymns every Sunday.

sentence: He taimaha rawa tēnei kete rīwai, kāore e taea e au te hiki.
translation: This sack of potatoes is far too heavy — I can't lift it.

sentence: Kua taimaha tōku ngākau mai i te matenga o tōku hoa rangatira.
translation: My heart has been heavy ever since my husband passed away.

sentence: Ia ahiahi ka haereere māua ko taku kurī i te tahataha o te awa.
translation: Every evening my dog and I stroll along the bank of the river.

sentence: I haereere mātou i ngā tāone iti o te Tai Rāwhiti i te raumati.
translation: We wandered around the small towns of the East Coast over the summer.

sentence: Kaua e haereere noa i te pō, kei ngaro koe i te ngahere.
translation: Don't go wandering about at night — you could get lost in the bush.

sentence: Ka whakawahi te minita i te kīngi hou ki te hinu tapu.
translation: The minister anoints the new king with the sacred oil.

sentence: Ka whakawahi taku whaea i tōku tuarā mamae ki te hinu wera.
translation: My mother rubs warm oil into my aching back.

sentence: Ki ahau nei, mā te iwi tonu e whakawahi tō rātou ake rangatira.
translation: The way I see it, it is for the people themselves to anoint their own leader.

sentence: I take mai tōku ingoa i tētahi tupuna i haere mai i Hawaiki.
translation: My name comes down from an ancestor who made the voyage from Hawaiki.

sentence: E ai ki te kaiako, ka take mai tēnei kupu i te reo Rātini.
translation: According to the teacher, this word derives from Latin.

sentence: Ki tōku whakaaro, i take mai te riri o te whānau i te whenua.
translation: In my view, the family's falling-out started over the land.

sentence: Ka kari au i te māra i te ata nei kia whakatōkia ngā kūmara.
translation: I'll dig the garden over this morning so the kūmara can go in.

sentence: I kari ngā tāne i te rua hāngī i te taha o te wharekai.
translation: The men dug the hāngī pit beside the dining hall.

sentence: Kua kari anō taku kurī i taku māra putiputi, ka riri au.
translation: My dog has dug up my flower garden again, and I'm furious.

sentence: Ka tunua e taku tuahine he parāoa rewena mō te hui ā-whānau.
translation: My sister is baking rēwena bread for the family gathering.

sentence: I tono taku tuahine ki a au kia tae atu ki tāna whakapōtaetanga āpōpō.
translation: My sister asked me to come along to her graduation tomorrow.

sentence: Ko tāku mahi he tiaki i tōku tuahine, ahakoa kua pakeke kē ia.
translation: It's my job to look out for my sister, even though she's grown up now.

sentence: Tokotoru ōku tuāhine, ā, ko au anake te tama a ōku mātua.
translation: I have three sisters, and I'm my parents' only son.

sentence: Kei te wharekai ōku tuāhine e mahi ana i te kai mā ngā manuhiri.
translation: My sisters are in the dining hall preparing the food for the visitors.

sentence: Ka nui taku aroha ki ōku tuāhine, ahakoa e noho tawhiti ana rātou.
translation: I love my sisters dearly, even though they live a long way off.

sentence: Kua tukua iho tēnei hei tiki pounamu mai i tōku kuia ki a au.
translation: This greenstone hei tiki has been handed down to me from my grandmother.

sentence: Kei te whakairo tōku matua kēkē i tētahi tiki rākau mō te whare tūpuna.
translation: My uncle is carving a wooden tiki for the ancestral meeting house.

sentence: Ki ahau, he taonga tapu te tiki, ehara i te whakapaipai noa.
translation: To me a tiki is a sacred treasure, not just an ornament.

sentence: Kua utua te nama hiko e taku matua, nā reira ka kā ngā rama.
translation: Dad has paid the power bill, so the lights are on again.

sentence: Kāore anō ngā kaimahi kia utua mō ā rātou hāora mahi i tērā wiki.
translation: The workers still haven't been paid for the hours they put in last week.

sentence: Ki tōku koroua, me utua te kino ki te pai, kaua ki te riri.
translation: My grandfather holds that a wrong should be repaid with kindness, not with anger.

sentence: Ka manaakitia ngā manuhiri ki te kai me te wai wera i te wharekai.
translation: The visitors are looked after with food and a hot drink in the dining hall.

sentence: I manaakitia mātou e ngā tāngata whenua i te pō roa o te hui.
translation: The local people cared for us right through the long night of the gathering.

sentence: Kia manaakitia koe e ngā tūpuna i tō haerenga ki tāwāhi, e taku tama.
translation: May the ancestors watch over you on your journey overseas, my son.

sentence: Ka haere te hepara me āna kurī ki te kohikohi hipi i te puke.
translation: The shepherd sets off with his dogs to muster sheep up on the hill.

sentence: Kua hoki mai te hepara i te makariri, mākū katoa ōna kākahu.
translation: The shepherd has come in out of the cold with his clothes soaked through.

sentence: He tangata ngākau māhaki te hepara rā, e mōhio ana ia ki ia hipi.
translation: That shepherd is a gentle-hearted man; he knows every single sheep by sight.

sentence: Kia tūpato i te piko o te rori, he mania rawa i te ua.
translation: Take care at the bend in the road — it gets very slippery in the rain.

sentence: Kei te piko tuarua o te awa te wāhi hī ika o tōku pāpā.
translation: My father's fishing spot is at the second bend of the river.

sentence: I mataku au i ngā piko o te huarahi ki Whanganui i te pō.
translation: The bends on the road to Whanganui frightened me after dark.

sentence: Ia ata ka heke tōku whaea kēkē ki te puna ki te tiki wai.
translation: Every morning my aunt goes down to the spring to fetch water.

sentence: Kua maroke te puna o te kāinga, nō reira ka hoko wai mātou.
translation: The spring at home has dried up, so now we have to buy our water.

sentence: He puna mātauranga tō mātou kuia, ka mimiti taua puna ina wehe ia.
translation: Our grandmother is a wellspring of knowledge, and that spring runs dry when she goes.

sentence: Ka aru te kurī i te ngeru puta noa i te māra kūmara.
translation: The dog chases the cat right across the kumara garden.

sentence: He roa te aru a ngā pirihimana i te motukā tāhae i Kirikiriroa.
translation: The police pursuit of the stolen car through Hamilton went on a long time.

sentence: I te moemoeā, ka aru tētahi taniwha i a au i te awa pōuri.
translation: In the dream a taniwha came chasing after me down the dark river.

sentence: I hae ngā tataramoa i ōku waewae i te ara ki te puke.
translation: The brambles tore at my legs on the track up the hill.

sentence: I hae te kaituhi i tētahi whārangi, ka tuhi i tōna ingoa ki reira.
translation: The writer tore out a page and signed her name on it.

sentence: Ka hae te hau makariri i ōku pāpāringa i te marae ātea.
translation: The cold wind cuts at my cheeks out on the open marae courtyard.

sentence: Ko te whakangaro o te ngahere te mate nui o tō mātou takiwā.
translation: The destruction of the forest is the biggest trouble facing our district.

sentence: I kōrero ngā kaumātua mō te whakangaro o ngā pā tawhito i te pakanga.
translation: The elders spoke about the destruction of the old fortified villages during the war.

sentence: Kua whakangaro te waipuke i te whare me te māra o tōku matua kēkē.
translation: The flood has wiped out my uncle's house and his garden with it.

sentence: He rahi ngā rīwai o tā mātou māra, ka hoatu ētahi ki ngā hoa.
translation: There are so many potatoes from our garden that we give some away to friends.

sentence: I tēnei tau, kua rahi ake ngā ākonga e ako ana i te reo.
translation: This year there are far more students learning the language.

sentence: Ahakoa he iti tō mātou hapū, he rahi te aroha i te wharenui.
translation: Our sub-tribe may be small, but there is no shortage of love in the meeting house.

sentence: Ka mau te kaikōrero i tōna tokotoko i a ia e whaikōrero ana.
translation: The speaker holds his carved staff while he delivers the formal address.

sentence: Ka whakawhirinaki tōku whaea ki tōna tokotoko ina piki ia i ngā arapiki.
translation: My mother leans on her walking stick whenever she climbs the stairs.

sentence: He taonga tuku iho tērā tokotoko, nā tōku tupuna i whakairo i mua.
translation: That staff is a family heirloom — my ancestor carved it long ago.

sentence: I te tōnga o te marama, ka pōuri rawa te huarahi ki te awa.
translation: Once the moon had gone down, the track to the river turned pitch dark.

sentence: E kore te pōwhiri e tū i muri i te tōnga o te rā.
translation: A pōwhiri is never held after the sun has set.

sentence: Ki ahau, ko te tōnga o te rā i Muriwai te mea ātaahua rawa.
translation: For me, the sunset at Muriwai is the most beautiful thing there is.

sentence: Kua kapi te rangi i ngā kapua, kāore au e whakairi i ngā kākahu.
translation: The sky has clouded right over, so I'm not hanging the washing out.

sentence: Ka huna ngā kapua i te tihi o Taranaki, ka whakakorea te hīkoi.
translation: The cloud hid the summit of Taranaki, so the climb was called off.

sentence: Ehara tērā i te kapua, he auahi kē nō te ngahere e wera ana.
translation: That's not a cloud — it's smoke from the forest burning.

sentence: Ka tunu a Pita i te kai mā te whānau i ia Rātapu.
translation: Pita cooks the meal for the family every Sunday.

sentence: Ko Pita te kaiwhakahaere o te tīma whutupōro i tō mātou kura.
translation: Pita is the manager of the rugby team at our school.

sentence: I tino pōuri a Pita i te ngaronga o tāna kurī i te ngahere.
translation: Pita was heartbroken when his dog went missing in the bush.

sentence: Kua ngoikore te rongonga o tōku koroua, nō reira ka kaha ake taku reo.
translation: My grandfather's hearing has faded, so I raise my voice for him.

sentence: Ka whakamātauria te rongonga o ngā tamariki i te tīmatanga o te tau.
translation: The children's hearing is tested at the beginning of the school year.

sentence: I tōku rongonga i te karanga, ka heke ngā roimata i ōku kanohi.
translation: The moment I heard the karanga, the tears ran down my face.

sentence: Ka whāngaihia te hau o te ika tuatahi ki a Tangaroa i te tahatai.
translation: The essence of the first fish is offered up to Tangaroa there on the shore.

sentence: Kei roto i te whakairo te hau o te tangata nāna i tārai.
translation: The essence of the man who carved it still lives inside the carving.

sentence: Ki tā te kōrero, ka hoki te hau o te koha ki tōna kaituku.
translation: As the saying goes, the essence of a gift makes its way back to the giver.

sentence: Ka karakia mātou i mua i te kai, ahakoa te hiakai o ngā tamariki.
translation: We say grace before we eat, however hungry the children are.

sentence: I karakia te kaumātua i te atatū, kātahi ka huakina te whare hou.
translation: The elder recited the karakia at first light, and only then was the new house opened.

sentence: Ia pō ka karakia au mō tōku whaea e takoto ana i te hōhipera.
translation: Every night I pray for my mother, who is lying in hospital.

sentence: Ka haere tō mātou whānau ki te temepara i Kirikiriroa i ia marama.
translation: Our family travels to the temple in Hamilton once a month.

sentence: I whakangaromia te temepara o Hiruhārama e ngā hōia o Roma.
translation: The temple in Jerusalem was destroyed by the Roman soldiers.

sentence: Ka noho puku au i roto i te temepara, ka mārama taku hinengaro.
translation: I sit in silence inside the temple and my mind clears.

sentence: He reka ake ngā hua piki o te rākau i ērā o te toa.

sentence: Kia tūpato ina whiti koe i te huarahi i mua i te kura.

sentence: Kua whiti te rā i muri i ngā rā ua, kua koa mātou.

sentence: Ka iri ngā pekapeka i ngā peka o te rākau i te pō.

sentence: He merekara i ora ai te ngeru i muri i te aituā waka.
translation: It is a miracle that the cat survived after the car crash.

sentence: I kauwhau te minita mō ngā merekara a Ihu i te Rātapu.
translation: The minister preached about the miracles of Jesus on Sunday.

sentence: Kāore au e whakapono ki ngā merekara, engari he mīharo tonu tēnei.
translation: I don't believe in miracles, but this is astonishing all the same.

sentence: Kua tunua e Māmā he keke tiakarete mō te huritau o taku teina.
translation: Mum has baked a chocolate cake for my little brother's birthday.

sentence: Ka mauria e ngā whaea he keke ki te hui ā-marae ia Rātapu.
translation: The women take a cake along to the marae gathering every Sunday.

sentence: Ahakoa i taka taku keke ki te papa, i kainga tonu e ngā tamariki.
translation: Even though my cake fell on the floor, the children ate it anyway.

sentence: Kei te whakatika a Koro i tana kupenga pakaru i mua i te whare.
translation: Koro is mending his torn net out in front of the house.

sentence: Ka toia e mātou te kupenga ki uta, kī tonu i te kahawai.
translation: We hauled the net up onto the shore, brimming with kahawai.

sentence: Auē, kua motu anō te kupenga, ā, kua puta ngā ika katoa.
translation: Oh no, the net has torn again, and every last fish has got out.

sentence: I hinga ngā taiepa o Heriko i te tangi o ngā tētere.
translation: The walls of Jericho fell at the sound of the trumpets.

sentence: I kōrero te kaiako mō Heriko ki ngā tamariki i te kura Rātapu.
translation: The teacher told the children about Jericho at Sunday school.

sentence: Kei te moemoeā au ki te toro atu ki Heriko, ki ngā taiepa tawhito.
translation: I dream of getting to Jericho one day, to see those ancient walls.

sentence: I awhi te whaea i tana pēpi ki tōna uma kia mutu te tangi.
translation: The mother held her baby against her chest until the crying stopped.

sentence: Ka papaki ngā tāne i ō rātou uma i te wā o te haka.
translation: The men slapped their chests as they performed the haka.

sentence: Kua mamae tōku uma i te maremare, me haere pea au ki te tākuta.
translation: My chest aches from all this coughing; perhaps I should see the doctor.

sentence: Kaua e whakatangi i tō tuahine, kua ngenge kē ia i te haerenga.
translation: Don't make your sister cry — she's already worn out from the trip.

sentence: Nā te waiata a te kuia i whakatangi ngā manuhiri katoa i te marae.
translation: The old woman's song made every one of the visitors on the marae cry.

sentence: Ko taua kiriata anake te mea e whakatangi ana i tōku pāpā.
translation: That film is the only thing that ever makes my dad cry.

sentence: I te pikinga o te maunga, ka poto haere tōku hā.
translation: As I climbed the mountain, my breath grew shorter and shorter.

sentence: Ka hongi māua ko te kuia, ka honoa ō māua hā i te whakatau.
translation: The kuia and I pressed noses, our breath joining at the welcome.

sentence: Hā! Kua mau koe i ahau, e kai ana i te keke!
translation: Ha! I've caught you red-handed eating the cake!

sentence: I whakanui au i te whakaahua o tōku kuia hei whakairi ki te pakitara.
translation: I enlarged the photograph of my grandmother so it could hang on the wall.

sentence: Me whakanui te tuhinga o te pānui kia kite ai ngā kaumātua.
translation: The writing on the notice needs enlarging so the elders can see it.

sentence: Nā te tangi o te pūtātara i whakanui te wehi o te pōwhiri.
translation: The call of the conch shell magnified the awe of the welcome ceremony.

sentence: I wiri a Pāpā i te papa rākau kia uru ai te taura.
translation: Dad drilled through the plank so the rope could pass through.

sentence: Kei te wiri ngā kaimahi i te pakitara mō ngā waea hiko.
translation: The workers are drilling into the wall for the electrical wiring.

sentence: Ka mataku au ina wiri te tākuta niho i taku niho kino.
translation: I get frightened whenever the dentist drills my bad tooth.

sentence: I tāwāhi nei, kei te manako au ki ngā kai a tōku kuia.
translation: Out here overseas, I'm aching for my grandmother's cooking.

sentence: Kua roa te whānau e manako ana kia hoki mai ngā tamariki.
translation: The family has spent a long time yearning for the children to come home.

sentence: Ka manako tōku ngākau ki ngā ahiahi raumati i te taha o te awa.
translation: My heart still longs for those summer evenings down by the river.

sentence: He mea hira ki tōku whaea kia noho tahi te whānau ki te kai.
translation: It matters a great deal to my mother that the family sits down to eat together.

sentence: Ka kōrerotia te take hira mō te whenua ki te marae āpōpō.
translation: The important land issue will be discussed at the marae tomorrow.

sentence: Kāore te tamaiti i te mōhio ki te hira o tēnei taonga tuku iho.
translation: The child has no idea how much this heirloom means.

sentence: Kua kī tōku manawa i te hāngī, kāore au e kai anō.
translation: My belly is full of hāngī; I'm not eating another thing.

sentence: Ko te marae te manawa o te hapū, ka huihui katoa mātou ki reira.
translation: The marae is the heart of the sub-tribe; that is where we all gather.

sentence: Kua pāngia tōku pāpā e te mate manawa, nō reira e māharahara ana mātou.
translation: My father has come down with heart disease, so we are all worried.

sentence: Ka haurangi a Rewi i te mārena, ka waiata ia i te pō katoa.
translation: Rewi got drunk at the wedding and sang the whole night through.

sentence: Kaua e taraiwa ina haurangi koe; waea mai, ka tiki atu au.
translation: Don't drive when you're drunk; ring me and I'll come and get you.

sentence: I pōuri tōku kuia i tana kitenga i ngā mokopuna kua haurangi.
translation: My grandmother was heartbroken to see the grandchildren drunk.

sentence: Kei te tunu keke a Hera mō te rā whānau o tana tamaiti āpōpō.
translation: Hera is baking a cake for her child's birthday tomorrow.

sentence: Ka tū a Hera hei kaikaranga mō tō mātou kura ā te Rāhoroi.
translation: Hera will stand as the caller for our school on Saturday.

sentence: Kāore a Hera i te hiahia ki te kōrero, i mate tana ngeru inanahi.
translation: Hera doesn't feel like talking; her cat died yesterday.

sentence: Ka pani a Māmā i te pata ki te parāoa mā ngā tamariki.
translation: Mum spreads the butter on the bread for the children.

sentence: Ka pani mātou i te whare karakia ki te peita hou ā te Rāhoroi.
translation: We're putting a coat of fresh paint on the church this Saturday.

sentence: Me pani te hinu ārai rā ki ngā tamariki, kei wera rātou.
translation: Rub the sunscreen on the children, or they'll get burnt.

sentence: I te hīkoi ngahere, ka rongo mātou i te kakara o te pere.
translation: On the bush walk we caught the scent of the karapapa.

sentence: Kua whakatōkia e ngā tamariki ētahi pere ki te taha o te awa.
translation: The children have planted karapapa along the edge of the river.

sentence: Ki tā tōku koroua, ko te pere te rākau kakara rawa o te ngahere.
translation: My grandfather reckons the karapapa is the most fragrant shrub in the forest.

sentence: I horo te kurī i te puaretanga o te kēti, kāore anō kia hoki.
translation: The dog bolted the moment the gate opened, and it still hasn't come back.

sentence: I te whakamā au, nō reira i horo au ki waho o te wharenui.
translation: I was mortified, so I fled outside the meeting house.

sentence: I whakataka te hoiho i taku tuahine ki te paru o te huarahi.
translation: The horse threw my sister down into the mud of the track.

sentence: E kore te kīngi e whakataka i tōna tūranga, ahakoa ngā tono katoa.
translation: The king will not step down from his throne, no matter how many demands there are.

sentence: Kua whero ngā tōmato i te māra, me kohi e tāua āpōpō.
translation: The tomatoes in the garden have gone red — the two of us should pick them tomorrow.

sentence: Ka whakaatu te kaiwhakawā i te kāri whero, ka wehe atu te kaitākaro.
translation: The referee held up the red card, and the player walked off.

sentence: I whero ōku pāpāringa i te whakamā i taku warewaretanga i te waiata.
translation: My cheeks went red with embarrassment when I forgot the words of the song.

sentence: Horoia ō ringaringa i mua i te kai, kua paru i te māra.
translation: Wash your hands before you eat — they got filthy out in the garden.

sentence: I horoia ngā waka katoa e ngā ākonga hei kohi pūtea mō te haerenga.
translation: All the cars were washed by the students to raise money for the trip.

sentence: I te putanga i te urupā, ka horoia ō mātou ringa ki te wai.
translation: As we came out of the cemetery, our hands were washed with water.

sentence: He turi tōku koroua, nō reira me kaha te kōrero ki a ia.
translation: My grandfather is deaf, so you have to speak up when you talk to him.

sentence: Kua ako te kura katoa i te reo rotarota mō ngā tamariki turi.
translation: The whole school has learned sign language for the deaf children.

sentence: Ahakoa he turi taku tuahine, he toa ia ki te kapa haka.
translation: My sister may be deaf, but she is a star of the kapa haka group.

sentence: I te ata hukapapa, ka aranga te kohu i runga i te awa.
translation: On a frosty morning the mist came up off the river.

sentence: Ka aranga anō te take whenua i te hui o te hapū inapō.
translation: The land question came up again at the hapū meeting last night.

sentence: Nā ngā kura kaupapa i aranga anō ai te reo o ngā tūpuna.
translation: It was the kura kaupapa that brought our ancestors' language back to life.

sentence: I kohia he takoha e te hapori hei hanga i te whare karakia hou.
translation: The community collected donations to build the new church.

sentence: Kua oati te kamupene ki te tuku takoha ki te kura ia tau.
translation: The company has pledged to give the school a donation every year.

sentence: Ahakoa he iti te takoha a te kuia rā, he nui tōna ngākau.
translation: That old woman's gift was small, but her heart was big.

sentence: Kua kapi te huarahi i te hukarere, kāore e taea te haere.
translation: The road is buried under snow, and there is no getting through.

sentence: Kua kapi ngā tūru katoa o te wharenui i ngā manuhiri i te pōwhiri.
translation: Every seat in the meeting house was filled with visitors at the pōwhiri.

sentence: Kua kapi katoa taku wiki i ngā hui, kāore he wā mō taku whānau.
translation: My whole week is packed with meetings, and there's no time left for my family.

sentence: Kua taka te niho tuatahi o taku tamaiti, kei te harikoa ia.
translation: My child's first tooth has fallen out and he is over the moon.

sentence: Kua puhuki ngā niho o te kani, nō reira ka roa te tapahi rākau.
translation: The saw's teeth have gone blunt, so cutting the wood takes forever.

sentence: Ka whakaatu te kurī i ōna niho, ka mataku ngā tamariki, ka oma.
translation: The dog bared its teeth, and the children took fright and ran.

sentence: I rongo mātou i te haruru o te wairere, engari kāore anō kia kitea.
translation: We could hear the roar of the waterfall, but it was still out of sight.

sentence: I te haka, ka tū ōku huruhuru i te haruru o ngā waewae.
translation: During the haka my hair stood on end at the thunder of the feet.

sentence: Kāore au i moe i te haruru o ngā taraka i te huarahi nui.
translation: I didn't sleep a wink, with the rumble of the trucks on the main road.

sentence: Kua hemo tō mātou koroua i te pō, kua tangi te whānau katoa.
translation: Our grandfather passed away in the night, and the whole family has been mourning.

sentence: I hemo ngā reme e rua i te makariri, ka pōuri te kaipāmu.
translation: Two of the lambs died in the cold, and the farmer was heartsick.

sentence: Kua tata hemo au i te wera o te rā i te māra.
translation: I nearly passed out from the heat of the sun in the garden.

sentence: I te mutunga o te kura, ka tae mai ngā tamariki, kua hemokai katoa.
translation: When school finished the children got home, every one of them famished.

sentence: Kua hemokai ngā kaimahi o te marae, nō reira ka karanga te ringawera.
translation: The marae workers were starving, so the kitchen crew called them in.

sentence: Ki ahau, he mea whakamā te hemokai o ngā tamariki i tēnei whenua momona.
translation: To my mind, children going hungry in a country this rich is a disgrace.

sentence: Kua inumia te miraka katoa e ngā tamariki, kāore he toenga mō te parakuihi.
translation: The children have drunk all the milk, and there's none left for breakfast.

sentence: I muri i ngā whaikōrero, ka inumia te tī e ngā manuhiri katoa.
translation: Once the speeches were over, the visitors all drank their tea.

sentence: He reka rawa te kawhe, e toru ngā kapu i inumia e au.
translation: The coffee was so good that I got through three cups of it.

sentence: Kei te ako tāku tama i te reo Pāniora mō tāna haerenga ki Hiri.
translation: My son is learning Spanish for his trip to Chile.

sentence: Nō Hiri tō mātou kaiako hou, ka kōrero ia mō ngā maunga o reira.
translation: Our new teacher is from Chile, and she tells us about the mountains there.

sentence: I te rū whenua i Hiri, i āwangawanga mātou mō te whānau o Ana.
translation: When the earthquake hit Chile, we were worried sick about Ana's family.

sentence: I makaia e taku tama te whatu o te pītiti ki te māra.
translation: My son chucked the peach stone out into the garden.

sentence: I pakaru ngā tomato a Koro i te ua whatu o te pō rā.
translation: Koro's tomatoes were smashed by the hail that fell that night.

sentence: He paitini te whatu o te karaka, koia i tūpato ai ngā mātua.
translation: The kernel of the karaka berry is poisonous, which is why parents keep such a close watch.

sentence: Māu e whakamahara mai ki a au kia hoko miraka i te toa.
translation: Remind me to buy milk while I'm at the shop, would you.

sentence: Ka tū te hui ā tērā marama hei whakamahara i ngā hōia i hinga.
translation: A gathering will be held next month to commemorate the soldiers who fell.

sentence: Ka whakamahara mai te kakara o te rēwena i a au ki tōku kuia.
translation: The smell of rēwena bread always brings my grandmother back to me.

sentence: Ia ata ka ahu a Kui i tāna māra rongoā, ahakoa te makariri.
translation: Every morning Kui tends her medicinal garden, however cold it is.

sentence: Kua rua tau te whānau nei e ahu ana i ngā tamariki whāngai tokorua.
translation: This family has been caring for two foster children for two years now.

sentence: He mea nui kia ahu tonu tātou i te reo o ō tātou tīpuna.
translation: It matters that we keep nurturing the language of our ancestors.

sentence: Kei te whakairo te tohunga i ngā epa hou mō te whare tupuna.
translation: The master carver is carving new wall panels for the ancestral house.

sentence: I moe mātou i te taha o ngā epa i te pō rā.
translation: That night we slept alongside the carved wall posts.

sentence: Ka rongo au i te wehi ina titiro atu ki ngā epa whakairo.
translation: A kind of awe comes over me whenever I look up at the carved wall posts.

sentence: I mate tōku tupuna i te Pakanga Tuarua o te Ao, i Kariti.
translation: My great-grandfather died in the Second World War, in Crete.

sentence: Kei te ako ngā tamariki mō ngā pakanga o Waikato i te karaehe hītori.
translation: The children are learning about the Waikato wars in their history class.

sentence: Kāore he painga o te pakanga, ko ngā tamariki te hunga e mamae ana.
translation: No good comes of war; it is the children who end up hurting.

sentence: Kei tua o te whare te wahie, tikina mai kia mura ai te ahi.
translation: The firewood is round the back of the house — go and get some to keep the fire going.

sentence: Ka rapua e Hone ngā hipi i tua o te puke i te ua.
translation: Hone went out in the rain to look for the sheep on the far side of the hill.

sentence: Ahakoa kei tua o te ārai ōku tūpuna, ka rangona tonu ō rātou reo.
translation: Though my ancestors have passed beyond the veil, their voices can still be heard.

sentence: Ka heke mātou ki te awaawa ki te tiki wai mō te puni.
translation: We headed down into the gully to fetch water for the camp.

sentence: He uaua ki ngā kaimahi te whakatū taiepa i ngā awaawa o te pāmu.
translation: Putting up fences in the farm's gullies is hard going for the crew.

sentence: I te hōtoke, ka ngaro wawe te rā i te awaawa, ka mātaotao mātou.
translation: In winter the sun leaves the valley early and we're left in the cold.

sentence: Homai te koko rā kia riringihia e au te hupa ki ngā oko.
translation: Pass me that ladle so I can serve the soup into the bowls.

sentence: I mauria mai e Koro tāna koko hei keri i te rua hāngī.
translation: Koro brought his own spade along to dig the hāngī pit.

sentence: Ahakoa kua whati te kakau, kāore a Pāpā e whakaae kia makaia tāna koko.
translation: The handle has snapped, but Dad still won't hear of his spade being thrown out.

sentence: Ia ahiahi, ka pānui tōku kuia i ngā kōrero Paipera mō Heperona.
translation: Every evening my grandmother reads the Bible stories about Hebron.

sentence: I te akomanga hītori, ka pātai mātou he aha i tapu ai a Heperona.
translation: In history class we asked why Hebron is a holy city.

sentence: Ka pōuri au ina rongo au i ngā kōrero mō ngā raruraru i Heperona.
translation: It saddens me whenever I hear the news about the troubles in Hebron.

sentence: Ka tīkina e mātou te wai māori mai i te puna o te kāinga.
translation: We fetch fresh water from the spring back at the home settlement.

sentence: He rā māori noa tēnei, engari ka tae mai te manuhiri i te ahiahi.
translation: This is an utterly ordinary day, but visitors arrive this afternoon.

sentence: Ehara tēnei wera i te mea māori; kua maroke ngā māra a ngā koroua.
translation: This heat is not normal — the old men's gardens have dried right out.

sentence: Ka maka a Pāpā i te aho ki te wai, ka tatari roa mātou.
translation: Dad casts the fishing line into the water, and we wait a long while.

sentence: Kei te whakatika ngā kaumātua i ngā aho o te kupenga i te takutai.
translation: The elders are down at the shore mending the cords of the net.

sentence: I tangi te tamaiti i te motunga o te aho o tana manu tukutuku.
translation: The little boy cried when the string of his kite snapped.

sentence: Ka mutu te nohopuku ina tō te rā, kātahi ka kai tahi te whānau.
translation: The fast ends when the sun goes down, and then the family eats together.

sentence: Kua whakaae ngā kaumātua ki te nohopuku hei whakanui i te rā tapu.
translation: The elders have agreed to fast as a way of honouring the holy day.

sentence: He uaua ki a au te nohopuku, engari ka māmā ake ina karakia mātou.
translation: Fasting is hard for me, but it gets easier once we pray together.

sentence: Ia Kirihimete ka waiatatia e te whānau ngā waiata mō Meri me tana pēpi.
translation: Every Christmas the family sings the carols about Mary and her baby.

sentence: I tū tāku tamāhine hei Meri i te whakaari Kirihimete a te kura.
translation: My daughter played Mary in the school's Christmas nativity play.

sentence: Ka miharo au ki a Meri mō tana kaha i ngā wā pōuri.
translation: I marvel at Mary for the strength she showed in the darkest times.

sentence: Ka hiki tōku māmā i te pēpi ki tōna hope, ka tunu kai ia.
translation: Mum swings the baby onto her hip and carries on cooking.

sentence: Ka mau ngā ringa ki te hope, ka tīmata te haka a ngā tāne.
translation: Hands go to the hips, and the men's haka begins.

sentence: Ka aroha au ki tōku kuia, kua piko tōna tuarā, ka mamae tōna hope.
translation: My heart goes out to my grandmother — her back is bent and her hips ache.

sentence: Nā ō mātou hoa nō Repanona i homai tētahi keke reka i te Kirihimete.
translation: Our friends from Lebanon brought us a delicious cake at Christmas.

sentence: I te kura, ka mātakitaki mātou i tētahi hōtaka mō ngā hita o Repanona.
translation: At school we watched a documentary about the cedars of Lebanon.

sentence: Ka āwangawanga tōku hoa mahi mō tōna whānau e noho ana i Repanona.
translation: My workmate frets about his family still living in Lebanon.

sentence: Ka kohia e ngā tamariki ngā huruhuru kererū i raro i ngā rākau.
translation: The children collect wood-pigeon feathers from under the trees.

sentence: Ka whatua e ngā wāhine ngā huruhuru kiwi ki te korowai mō te tangi.
translation: The women weave the kiwi feathers into the cloak for the funeral.

sentence: Kua kapi te whāriki i ngā huruhuru o te kurī, ka riri tōku māmā.
translation: The carpet is covered in dog hair, and Mum is furious.

sentence: Ka wehe a Māmā i te kēke ki ngā wāhanga e ono mā mātou.
translation: Mum divides the cake into six pieces for us.

sentence: Ka wehe te kaiako i ngā tamariki kia rua ngā rōpū mō te tākaro.
translation: The teacher splits the children into two teams for the game.

sentence: Ka wehe ngā manuhiri i te marae, ka waiata poroporoaki mātou ki a rātou.
translation: As the visitors leave the marae, we sing them a farewell.

sentence: I puta te heihei i te taiapa, ka hopu taku teina i a ia.
translation: The chicken got out through the fence, and my younger brother caught it.

sentence: Ka hopu te kaitākaro i te pōro, ka umere te hunga mātakitaki katoa.
translation: The player catches the ball, and the whole crowd roars.

sentence: I hopu taku koroua i tētahi tuna i te awa, ka kata koa ia.
translation: My grandfather caught an eel in the river and laughed with delight.

sentence: Mai i te aonga ki te pō, ka mahi mātou i te māra kūmara.
translation: From first light until dark we worked in the kūmara garden.

sentence: I te aonga o te rā, ka hoe ngā kaihī ika ki te moana.
translation: At daybreak the fishermen paddled out to sea.

sentence: Nō te aonga ake o te rā, ka kitea te kino o te tupuhi.
translation: Only when day broke the next morning could we see how bad the storm had been.

sentence: Ka hui te whānau ki te wharekai ia Rātapu mō te hākari.
translation: The family gathers in the dining hall every Sunday for the shared meal.

sentence: I hui ngā kaimahi ki te wharenui ki te whiriwhiri i te take whenua.
translation: The workers met in the meeting house to thrash out the land question.

sentence: Nō te matenga o te kuia, ka hui mai te hapū ki te poroporoaki.
translation: When the old woman died, the whole hapū gathered to farewell her.

sentence: I ahatia tō ringa, i takaia ai ki te kākahu mā?
translation: What happened to your arm, that it's been wrapped up in white cloth?

sentence: Kaua e ahatia ngā whakairo o te wharenui, he tapu ērā ki te iwi.
translation: Don't lay a finger on the carvings in the meeting house — they are sacred to the tribe.

sentence: E āwangawanga ana a Māmā, kei ahatia tana tama i te tāone nui.
translation: Mum is anxious that something will happen to her son in the big city.

sentence: I whānau a Ihu ki Peterehema i te wā o te kīngitanga o Herora.
translation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem during the reign of King Herod.

sentence: Ka tae te rōpū hāhi ki Peterehema i te Kirihimete, ka waiata rātou.
translation: The church group arrives in Bethlehem at Christmas, and there they sing.

sentence: He iti a Peterehema, engari kei te mōhio te ao katoa ki tōna ingoa.
translation: Bethlehem is a small place, yet the whole world knows its name.

sentence: Kei te moe te pēpi i te awatea, ka oho i te waenganui pō.
translation: The baby sleeps right through the daylight and then wakes in the middle of the night.

sentence: I tāhaetia te motukā i te awatea tonu, i te aroaro o te katoa.
translation: The car was stolen in broad daylight, right in front of everyone.

sentence: He poto rawa te awatea i te takurua, kāore e oti aku mahi.
translation: There is far too little daylight in winter — I never get my work finished.

sentence: Ka haere tōku pāpā ki te rūnanga āpōpō ki te kōrero mō te awa.
translation: My father is going to the council tomorrow to speak about the river.

sentence: Nā te rūnanga i whakaae kia hangaia he kura hou mō ngā tamariki.
translation: It was the council that agreed a new school should be built for the children.

sentence: Kāore te rūnanga i whakarongo ki ā mātou tono, nā reira ka riri mātou.
translation: The council would not listen to our requests, and that is why we were angry.

sentence: Kei ngā kuia te whakahaere o te kīhini i te wā o te tangihanga.
translation: The kuia have charge of running the kitchen during the funeral.

sentence: Kua tāia ngā whakahaere o te rā ki te pepa mō ngā manuhiri.
translation: The day's order of proceedings has been printed on paper for the visitors.

sentence: He pai te whakahaere o te hui, kāore he raruraru i puta.
translation: The meeting was well run — not a single problem came up.

sentence: Kua roa ōku makawe, me tapahi e Māmā ā te Rāhoroi nei.
translation: My hair has got long; Mum should cut it this coming Saturday.

sentence: Ka whiria e ngā māmā ngā makawe o ngā kōtiro mō te kapa haka.
translation: The mothers plait the girls' hair for the kapa haka performance.

sentence: Kua hina ngā makawe o tōku koroua, engari kāore anō ia kia ngoikore.
translation: My grandfather's hair has gone grey, but he has not weakened yet.

sentence: I hinga au i tētahi pakiaka rākau i te ara ki te awa.
translation: I tripped over a tree root on the track down to the river.

sentence: Kāore i taea te parau, he maha rawa ngā pakiaka i te māra.
translation: We couldn't plough: there were far too many roots in the garden.

sentence: Kua hinga te tōtara, engari kei te ora tonu ōna pakiaka i raro.
translation: The tōtara has fallen, but its roots are still alive down below.

sentence: I ware au ki te kati i te kēti, ā, kua puta ngā hipi.
translation: I carelessly left the gate unlatched, and now the sheep have got out.

sentence: Ka ware au ki ngā kōrero o te hui, ka whakaaro ki te kāinga.
translation: My mind drifted away from the speeches at the meeting and back home.

sentence: Kia tūpato, kaua e ware ina whakawhiti koe i te huarahi.
translation: Be careful — don't let your attention wander when you cross the road.

sentence: Ka kaukau ngā tamariki i te manga i muri i te marae ia raumati.
translation: The children swim in the creek behind the marae every summer.

sentence: I tapahia e ngā kaimahi te manga i taka ki te huarahi inapō.
translation: The workers cut up the branch that came down on the road last night.

sentence: E pōuri ana au, kua paru te manga i inu ai mātou i mua.
translation: It saddens me that the stream we used to drink from has gone dirty.

sentence: I horoia e tōku kuia te motu i taku turi ki te wai mahana.
translation: My grandmother washed the cut on my knee with warm water.

sentence: Ka whakawhiti mātou ki te motu ā te ata ki te whakatō rākau.
translation: We cross over to the island in the morning to plant trees.

sentence: E āwangawanga ana tōku whaea, kāore anō te motu i taku ringa kia ora.
translation: My mother is worried — the cut on my hand still hasn't healed.

sentence: I kati ngā namu i ō māua waewae i te taha o te awa.
translation: The sandflies bit our legs down by the river.

sentence: Ka kati te ika i te maunu, kātahi ka hikina e taku tuakana.
translation: The fish took the bait, and then my older brother hauled it in.

sentence: Kaua e whakapā atu ki taua kurī pango, ka kati i tō ringa.
translation: Don't touch that black dog — it will bite your hand.

sentence: Ka amo mai te puru i te pārae, ka oma mātou ki te taiapa.
translation: The bull charged at us across the paddock and we ran for the fence.

sentence: I amo te ope taua ki te pā i te atatū o taua rā.
translation: The war party charged the pā at first light that day.

sentence: Ka amo te kaitākaro ki te raina, ka hamama te hunga mātakitaki.
translation: The player charged for the line and the crowd roared.

sentence: Kua pihi ngā kākano i whakatōkia e tāua i te māra i tērā marama.
translation: The seeds the two of us planted in the garden last month have sprouted.

sentence: Kei te titiro ngā kaumātua mēnā kua pihi ngā kūmara i te māra.
translation: The elders are checking whether the kūmara have come up in the garden.

sentence: Kua pihi anō te reo i ngā kōhanga reo, ā, e koa ana au.
translation: The language has sprung up again in the kōhanga reo, and that delights me.

sentence: Kua whakatuwhera tētahi whānau nō Hiria i tētahi toa parāoa i tō mātou tāone.
translation: A family from Syria has opened a bakery in our town.

sentence: I tohua e te kaiako te wāhi o Hiria i te mahere whenua.
translation: The teacher pointed out where Syria was on the map.

sentence: E pōuri ana au mō ngā tamariki o Hiria kua ngaro ō rātou kāinga.
translation: I feel for the children of Syria whose homes have been lost.

sentence: I tapaina te pēpi ko Hopa, he ingoa i heke mai i tōna koroua.
translation: The baby was named Hopa, a name handed down from his grandfather.

sentence: Ka whakatangi a Hopa i tāna kitā i te whare tupuna ia Rāhoroi.
translation: Hopa plays his guitar in the meeting house every Saturday.

sentence: Ka maumahara au ki te manawanui o Hopa i ngā wā uaua.
translation: I remember Job's patience when times are hard.

sentence: Kua pirau ngā rīwai i wareware i a au i roto i te kāpata.
translation: The potatoes I forgot about in the cupboard have gone rotten.

sentence: Kāore taku tama e kai i te aporo, e kī ana ia he pirau.
translation: My son won't eat the apple; he reckons it's rotten.

sentence: Neke atu, kāore au e kite i te pouaka whakaata i a koe.

sentence: Me neke e tātou ngā tūru ki te wharekai i mua i te hui.
translation: We should shift the chairs into the dining hall before the meeting.

sentence: I neke au ki te taha kia noho ai te kuia i te pahi.
translation: I moved along so the old woman could sit down on the bus.

sentence: Ka mataku taku tama i te whatitiri, ka oma ia ki tō māua moenga.
translation: My son gets frightened by the thunder and runs to our bed.

sentence: I mataku au ki te whaikōrero i mua i ngā kaumātua i te marae.
translation: I was afraid to make a formal speech in front of the elders at the marae.

sentence: Kāore au e mataku ki te pōuri, engari ka mataku au ki ngā pūngāwerewere.

sentence: I taku huakanga i te pouaka mātao, ka puta te haunga o te kina.

sentence: Ka whakarērea e ngā kaimahi te wharekai i te haunga o te para.

sentence: Ahakoa te haunga o te tītī, koinei te kai tino reka ki a Koro.
translation: Despite the stench of muttonbird, it is Koro's absolute favourite food.

sentence: Me tote koe i ngā ika i mua i te whakairi ki te rā.
translation: You should salt the fish before you hang them out in the sun.

sentence: I totea ngā tuna e ngā kuia mō te hui ā tērā wiki.
translation: The kuia salted the eels for next week's gathering.

sentence: Kua tote rawa koe i te hupa, ka mate mātou i te hiainu.
translation: You have over-salted the soup — now we will all be dying of thirst.

sentence: Kua pukupuku te hupa, nā te mea kāore koe i āta konatunatu.
translation: The soup has gone lumpy because you did not stir it carefully.

sentence: Ina marino te whanga i te ata, ka haere mātou ki te hī ika.
translation: When the bay is calm in the morning, we go out fishing.

sentence: Ka whakawhiti mātou i te whanga mā runga poti kia tae ki te marae.
translation: We cross the bay by boat so we can get to the marae.

sentence: I noho au ki te pari, mātakitaki ai i ngā tohorā i te whanga.
translation: I sat up on the cliff, watching the whales out in the bay.

sentence: Kua kī taku kete i ngā rīwai hou mai i te māra a Koro.
translation: My basket is full of new potatoes from Koro's garden.

sentence: Kei te raranga a Mere i tētahi kete harakeke hei koha mō te manuhiri.
translation: Mere is weaving a flax basket as a gift for the visitors.

sentence: He taonga tuku iho tēnei kete, nā tōku kuia i raranga i mua.
translation: This basket is a family heirloom — my grandmother wove it years ago.

sentence: I te mutunga o te kēmu kāri, ka whakatakotoria e Koro tāna hai.
translation: At the end of the card game, Koro laid down his ace.

sentence: E toru ngā hai i tōku ringa, engari kāore au i te kōrero.
translation: There are three aces in my hand, but I am saying nothing.

sentence: Nā tāna hai i toa ai a Hēmi, ā, ka umere te whānau katoa.
translation: It was his ace that won it for Hēmi, and the whole family cheered.

sentence: Kāore he oki i a mātou i te wā o te hauhake kūmara.
translation: We got no rest at all during the kūmara harvest.

sentence: I muri i te whakangungu, ka tukuna he oki poto ki ngā kaihoe.
translation: After the training session the paddlers were given a short rest.

sentence: Kua ngenge rawa au, ko te oki anake taku hiahia i tēnei rangi.
translation: I am completely worn out — all I want today is a rest.

sentence: Nā te aitua i te huarahi, i tōmuri ai mātou ki te tangihanga.
translation: Because of the accident on the road, we arrived late to the funeral.

sentence: Me mau pōtae mārō i te wāhi hanga, kei pā he aitua.
translation: Wear a hard hat on the building site, in case there is an accident.

sentence: I te rongonga o te whānau i te aitua, ka tangi te karanga.
translation: When the family heard of the tragedy, the karanga rang out in mourning.

sentence: Ko tōku tupuna te tangata nāna au i whāngai i tōku tamarikitanga.
translation: My grandfather is the one who raised me when I was a child.

sentence: I tapaina te wharenui ki te tupuna nāna te iwi i ārahi mai.
translation: The meeting house was named after the ancestor who led the tribe here.

sentence: Ka mihi tonu au ki tōku tupuna, nāna au i whakaako ki te whakairo.
translation: I still give thanks to my grandfather, who taught me to carve.

sentence: I ia pō, ka kōrero tōku pāpā ki a mātou mō ō mātou tūpuna.
translation: Every night my father tells us about our ancestors.

sentence: I te wānanga, ka whakaakona ngā tamariki ki ngā ingoa o ō rātou tūpuna.
translation: At the wānanga the children are taught the names of their ancestors.

sentence: Kei te mihi tonu mātou ki ngā tūpuna nā rātou i pupuri tēnei whenua.
translation: We still pay tribute to the ancestors who held on to this land.

sentence: Kua huri te hau ki te tonga, ka makariri te whare āpōpō.
translation: The wind has swung round to the south, so the house will be cold tomorrow.

sentence: I te hui, ka huri te kaikōrero ki a mātou, ka pātai mai.
translation: At the meeting the speaker turned round to face us and put a question to us.

sentence: I huri ahau ki muri, engari kua ngaro kē taku hoa i te mano.
translation: I turned around, but my friend had already vanished into the crowd.

sentence: I hono tōku pāpā i ngā paipa hou i raro i te whare inanahi.
translation: Yesterday my dad joined the new pipes together under the house.

sentence: I hono mai a Hēmi ki te hui ipurangi i tōna kāinga i Ōtautahi.
translation: Hēmi joined the online meeting from his home in Christchurch.

sentence: Nā te rangahau whakapapa i hono anō ai mātou ki ō mātou whanaunga ngaro.
translation: The whakapapa research reconnected us with the relatives we had lost touch with.

sentence: Kua mahaki taku tama, nō reira ka noho māua ki te kāinga āpōpō.
translation: My son has fallen ill, so the two of us will stay home tomorrow.

sentence: Ka toro te minita i ngā mahaki o te hōhipera i ia Rātapu.
translation: The minister visits the patients in the hospital every Sunday.

sentence: Ahakoa he mahaki ia, i haere tonu tōku kuia ki te tangihanga.
translation: Even though she was ill, my grandmother still went to the tangi.

sentence: Kei te tunu kai a Piripi mā tōna whānau i te kīhini.
translation: Philip is cooking a meal for his family in the kitchen.

sentence: I whakaakona e Piripi te kapa haka o tō mātou kura i tērā tau.
translation: Philip taught our school's kapa haka group last year.

sentence: I riri a Piripi i te mea kāore mātou i tatari ki a ia.
translation: Philip got angry because we didn't wait for him.

sentence: I te ata nei, i tanu māua ko taku kuia i ngā rīwai.
translation: This morning my grandmother and I planted the potatoes.

sentence: I tanu ngā tamariki i ngā kauri hei whakamaharatanga ki ō rātou tīpuna.
translation: The children planted kauri trees in memory of their ancestors.

sentence: E kī ana taku koroua, me tanu te kūmara i te wā o Matariki.
translation: My grandfather says the kūmara should go into the ground around Matariki.

sentence: I a mātou e hī ika ana, ka hiko te uira i te moana.
translation: While we were out fishing, lightning flashed over the sea.

sentence: Kua mate te uira i te āwhā, ka tunua ā mātou kai ki waho.
translation: The storm has knocked out the power, so our food was cooked outside.

sentence: Ka mataku taku teina i te uira, ka huna ki raro i te moenga.
translation: My little brother is frightened of the lightning and hides under the bed.

sentence: E maturuturu ana te ua i te tuanui ki runga i taku moenga.
translation: Rain is dripping through the roof onto my bed.

sentence: Ka mahi ngātahi ngā whānau ki te whakahou i te tuanui o te wharekai.
translation: The families are working together to replace the roof of the dining hall.

sentence: I ngā pō raumati, ka piki mātou ki te tuanui ki te mātakitaki whetū.
translation: On summer nights we would climb onto the roof to watch the stars.

sentence: I takai a Māmā i te pēpi ki te paraikete wūru, he makariri hoki.
translation: Mum wrapped the baby up in the woollen blanket, because it was cold.

sentence: Ka takai ngā kuia i ngā kai ki ngā rau harakeke mō te hāngī.
translation: The kuia wrap the food in flax leaves for the hāngī.

sentence: Ka takai te kaiako i tōku ringa, ā, ka mutu taku tangi.
translation: The teacher wrapped up my hand, and I stopped crying.

sentence: Ahakoa taku karanga, kāore taku tuakana i aro mai ki ahau.
translation: Though I called out, my older sister didn't turn round to me.

sentence: Me aro koutou ki te kaikōrero, kaua e kōrero i waenga i te hui.
translation: Pay attention to the speaker; don't talk in the middle of the meeting.

sentence: Nō te matenga o tōna pāpā, ka aro a Mere ki te whakairo rākau.
translation: After her father died, Mere turned to wood carving.

sentence: Ka taka ngā pata ua tuatahi ki te kirikiri, ka oma mātou ki roto.
translation: The first drops of rain hit the gravel and we ran inside.

sentence: E heke ana ngā pata werawera i te rae o te kaimahi hāngī.
translation: Beads of sweat are running down the forehead of the man working the hāngī.

sentence: Nā te pata o te kōrere i kore ai au e moe.
translation: The dripping of the tap was why I couldn't get to sleep.

sentence: I tunu kai mātou i te kāuta i te tangihanga o tōku kuia.
translation: We did the cooking in the kitchen throughout my grandmother's funeral.

sentence: Ka kati te tari āpōpō, nā te mea kei te tangihanga mātou katoa.
translation: The office will be shut tomorrow, because we will all be at the funeral.

sentence: I te tangihanga, ka mārama au ki te kaha o tōku whānau.
translation: It was at the funeral that I came to understand how strong my family is.

sentence: Ka kakau ngā tamariki i te awa i muri i te kura.
translation: The children swim in the river after school.

sentence: I whakaako tōku matua i a au ki te kakau i te moana.
translation: My father taught me to swim in the sea.

sentence: Ka mataku au ki te kakau ki tērā taha, he hōhonu rawa te awa.
translation: I am scared to swim to the far side, because the river is far too deep.

sentence: I whiu au i tētahi kōhatu ki te roto, ka wiki te wai.
translation: I threw a stone into the lake and the water rippled out in rings.

sentence: Ka rore mātou i ngā kiore i raro i te whare o tōku kuia.
translation: We trap the rats under my grandmother's house.

sentence: I rorea ngā paihamu e ngā kaimahi i te taha o te ara hīkoi.
translation: The workers trapped the possums along the side of the walking track.

sentence: Kāore au i pai ki te rore manu, engari he kai mā te whānau.
translation: I never liked snaring birds, but it puts food on the table for the family.

sentence: I pāngia tōku tuakana e te hore, ā, i pupuhi tōna kakī.
translation: My older brother came down with scrofula, and his neck swelled up.

sentence: Ka whakaora te tohunga i te hore ki ngā rau kawakawa o te ngahere.
translation: The tohunga treats scrofula with kawakawa leaves gathered from the forest.

sentence: I mataku te iwi ki te hore, nā te mea he roa te whakaora.
translation: People were afraid of scrofula, because recovering from it took so long.

sentence: I pānui tōku kuia i te kōrero mō Ihu o Nahareta i te ata.
translation: My grandmother read the story about Jesus of Nazareth this morning.

sentence: I toro mātou ki Nahareta i te wā i noho ai mātou ki Ihirāira.
translation: We visited Nazareth during the time we were living in Israel.

sentence: Ka waiata te hāhi mō te tamaiti o Nahareta i ia Kirihimete.
translation: The church sings about the child of Nazareth every Christmas.

sentence: I motu tōku maihao i te māripi i a au e tapahi aporo ana.
translation: I cut my finger on the knife while I was slicing apples.

sentence: Ka tohu te kaiako ki tōna maihao i te kupu hou kei te papatuhi.
translation: The teacher points with her finger at the new word on the board.

sentence: Kua pakari ngā maihao o tōku koroua i ngā tau mahi i te māra.
translation: My grandfather's fingers have grown hard from years of working in the garden.

sentence: Ka whakakī au i te ipu ki te miraka mā te ngeru ia ata.
translation: Every morning I fill the bowl with milk for the cat.

sentence: Ka riringi te kuia i te tī ki te ipu mā ngā manuhiri.
translation: The kuia pours the tea into the cup for the visitors.

sentence: Ka pupuri tonu au i te ipu a tōku whaea, ahakoa kua pakaru.
translation: I still keep my mother's cup, even though it is broken.

sentence: Ka nui haere ngā ngaru, nō reira ka hoki mātou ki uta.
translation: The waves kept getting bigger, so we headed back to shore.

sentence: Ka eke tōku tuakana i ngā ngaru o Whāingaroa i te raumati.
translation: My older brother rides the waves at Raglan over the summer.

sentence: Ka whakamārie te haruru o ngā ngaru i a au i te pō.
translation: The rumble of the waves settles me at night.

sentence: Ka tuku au i ngā whakaahua o te huritau ki tōku whaea āpōpō.
translation: I will send the birthday photos to my mother tomorrow.

sentence: I tango te kaiwhakaahua i tētahi whakaahua o te kapa haka i te mutunga.
translation: The photographer took a picture of the kapa haka group at the very end.

sentence: Ka titiro au ki ngā whakaahua o ō mātou tūpuna i te wharenui.
translation: I gaze at the photographs of our ancestors hanging in the meeting house.

sentence: Homai te hama, kei te hanga au i te taiapa mō ngā hipi.
translation: Pass me the hammer — I'm putting up the fence for the sheep.

sentence: Kei te rapu te kaihanga i tana hama i waenga i ngā rākau.
translation: The builder is hunting for his hammer somewhere in the pile of timber.

sentence: He taumaha rawa tēnei hama mō tāku tamāhine, kāore e taea te hiki.
translation: This hammer is far too heavy for my daughter — she can't even lift it.

sentence: Ia pō, ka tangi te ruru i te ngahere i muri i te whare.
translation: Every night the morepork calls from the bush behind the house.

sentence: Ka tatau ngā kaitiaki i ngā ruru o te ngahere i ia tau.
translation: The rangers count the moreporks in the forest every year.

sentence: E ai ki tōku kuia, he tohu aituā te tangi o te ruru.
translation: According to my grandmother, the morepork's call is a sign of misfortune coming.

sentence: I tono te kaiwhakahaere o te toa kia mahi au i te Rāhoroi.
translation: The manager of the shop asked me to come in and work on Saturday.

sentence: Ko Mere te kaiwhakahaere o te hui, nā reira e kore tātou e roa.
translation: Mere is running the meeting, so we won't be here long.

sentence: He ngākau māhaki tō mātou kaiwhakahaere, ahakoa te taumaha o te mahi.
translation: Our manager stays gentle with us, however heavy the work gets.

sentence: Ka whakapapa mātou i ngā rau harakeke ki runga i ngā kōhatu wera.
translation: We lay the flax leaves out flat over the hot stones.

sentence: Me whakapapa ngā papa rākau ki te taha o te whare kia maroke ai.
translation: The boards should be stacked flat beside the shed so they dry out.

sentence: Ka whakapapa te tamaiti ki raro i te moenga kia kore ai e kitea.
translation: The child lay flat under the bed so that nobody would find him.

sentence: Ka tae mai te tira o Ngāti Porou ki te marae i te ahiahi.
translation: The travelling party from Ngāti Porou reached the marae late in the afternoon.

sentence: Tekau mā rua ngā tāngata o tō mātou tira i haere ki Waitangi.
translation: Twelve of us in our party made the trip up to Waitangi.

sentence: Kua ngenge te tira i te hīkoi roa, nō reira ka whakatā mātou.
translation: The party is worn out after the long walk, so we're stopping to rest.

sentence: I ia raumati, ka haere mātou ki te takutai o Whangamatā ki te kaukau.

sentence: I te raumati, ka mahi ngā tauira ki ngā māra huarākau o Te Puke.
translation: Over the summer the students take work in the orchards around Te Puke.

sentence: He wera rawa te raumati o tērā tau, kāore mātou i moe pai.
translation: Last year's summer was so hot that none of us slept properly.

sentence: Kua pakari ngā hua o te rākau āporo, me kohi e tātou.
translation: The apples on the tree have ripened — we should get them picked.

sentence: Kua pakari haere te reo o ngā tamariki i te kura kaupapa Māori.
translation: The children's language has been steadily maturing at the Māori-language school.

sentence: Ahakoa he rangatahi tonu ia, kua pakari tana whaikōrero i te marae.
translation: Young as he still is, his speech-making on the marae has come of age.

sentence: Kei tua o te puke tō mātou kāinga, he hīkoi roa ki te kura.
translation: Our home sits on the far side of the hill, so it's a long walk to school.

sentence: Ia ata, ka peia e tōku pāpā ngā hipi ki runga i te puke.
translation: Every morning my father drives the sheep up onto the hill.

sentence: Ahakoa te ngenge, he ātaahua te tirohanga mai i runga i te puke.
translation: Tiring as the climb was, the view from the top of the hill is beautiful.

sentence: Kua kapi te māra i ngā taru, me ngaki e mātou āpōpō.

sentence: Ka kai ngā kau i te taru mātotoru i te taha o te awa.
translation: The cows graze on the thick grass along the edge of the river.

sentence: He pōuri au i ngā taru e tipu ana i runga i te urupā.
translation: It saddens me to see the weeds growing over the graves.

sentence: Kua pau te waituhi o tāku pene i te wā o te whakamātautau.

sentence: Homai tētahi pene kia tuhia e au tōku ingoa ki te rārangi.
translation: Hand me a pen so I can put my name down on the list.

sentence: He taonga tēnei pene ki ahau, nā tōku koroua i tuku mai.
translation: This pen means a great deal to me — my grandfather passed it on.

sentence: I keria e mātou ngā uhi i te māra i mua i te ua.
translation: We dug the yams out of the garden before the rain came.

sentence: I tunua ngā uhi ki roto i te hāngī mō te hui nui.
translation: The yams were cooked in the hāngī for the big gathering.

sentence: Ki tōku whakaaro, he reka ake te uhi i te rīwai i te takurua.
translation: To my mind, yam tastes better than potato in the middle of winter.

sentence: I tapaina tōku tuahine ko Rutu, he ingoa nō te Paipera.
translation: My sister was named Ruth, a name taken from the Bible.

sentence: I pānuitia e te minita te pukapuka a Rutu i te karakia.
translation: The minister read from the Book of Ruth during the church service.

sentence: I whai a Rutu i tōna hungawai ki tētahi whenua tauhou, ahakoa te mataku.

sentence: Kāore au i te whakaae kia tango te pākihi i ngā rākau tawhito.
translation: I don't accept the company taking away those old trees.

sentence: Kaua e wareware ki tō marara, kua tīmata kē te ua ki waho.
translation: Don't forget your umbrella — it has already started raining outside.

sentence: Nā tōku hoa mahi i homai tana marara i te tūnga pahi inanahi.
translation: My workmate handed me her umbrella at the bus stop yesterday.

sentence: He iti rawa tēnei marara, kua mākū kē ōku pakihiwi i te ua.
translation: This umbrella is far too small — my shoulders are already soaked.

sentence: Me whakaoti e koe ō mahi kāinga i mua i te tākaro.
translation: You need to finish your homework before you go off and play.

sentence: Kua whakaoti te rōpū i te whare hou i mua i te Kirihimete.
translation: The crew finished the new house before Christmas.

sentence: Kāore i taea e au te whakaoti i taku tuhinga, nā te ngenge.
translation: I couldn't finish my essay because I was too tired.

sentence: Kei te ako taku tamaiti i ngā ingoa o ngā awa katoa o Aotearoa.
translation: My child is learning the names of every river in Aotearoa.

sentence: Ka haere tō mātou kapa haka ki ngā whakataetae puta noa i Aotearoa.
translation: Our kapa haka group travels to competitions all over Aotearoa.

sentence: I taku hokinga ki Aotearoa, ka tangi au i te kite i ngā maunga.
translation: When I came home to Aotearoa, I wept at the sight of the mountains.

sentence: Kei te tunu parāoa a Hine mā tōna kuia i te ata nei.
translation: Hine is baking bread for her grandmother this morning.

sentence: Kua tohua a Hine hei kaikōrero mō te rōpū i te hui ā-kura.
translation: Hine has been chosen to speak for the group at the school meeting.

sentence: E hine, kaua e mataku — kei kō tō whaea e tatari ana.
translation: Don't be frightened, girl — your mother is waiting just over there.

sentence: I tito taku koroua i tētahi oriori mō tana mokopuna hou.
translation: My grandfather composed a lullaby for his new grandchild.

sentence: Kei te tito waiata te akomanga mō te whakataetae kapa haka ā tērā marama.
translation: The class is composing a song for next month's kapa haka competition.

sentence: Kaua e tito kōrero ki a au — kua mōhio kē au ki te pono.
translation: Don't make up stories for me — I already know the truth.

sentence: Nau mai ki roto, e hoa, kua rite kē te tī me te keke.
translation: Come on in, friend — the tea and cake are already waiting.

sentence: Nau mai, e te whanaunga — kua roa mātou e tatari ana ki a koe.
translation: Welcome, cousin — we have been waiting a long time for you.

sentence: Kei te tiaki taku kuia i ana whakaahua kahurangi i roto i te pouaka.
translation: My grandmother keeps her treasured photographs safe inside the box.

sentence: I ākina mātou e te tumuaki kia whāia te iti kahurangi i ia rā.
translation: The principal urged us to chase our highest aspiration every single day.

sentence: I kī te kaumātua, ko te reo te taonga kahurangi o tō mātou iwi.
translation: The elder said the language is our tribe's most precious treasure.

sentence: He teitei rawa te whata, nō reira ka piki taku tama ki te tūru.
translation: The shelf is far too high, so my son climbs up onto the chair.

sentence: Kei te hanga mātou i te taiepa kia teitei ake, kei oma ngā hipi.
translation: We're building the fence higher so the sheep don't get out.

sentence: Kāore au e kaha ki te tū i ngā wāhi teitei, ka wiri au.
translation: I can't stand being up high — I start shaking.

sentence: Me huhuti e koe ngā tarutaru o te māra i mua i te ua.
translation: You should pull the weeds out of the garden before the rain comes.

sentence: I muri i te ua, ka tipu tere ngā tarutaru i te papa tākaro.
translation: After the rain, the grass shot up all over the playing field.

sentence: Kua ngaro katoa aku riwai i raro i ngā tarutaru, e pōuri ana au.
translation: My potatoes have vanished completely under the weeds, and I'm gutted.
